system.name: Fomalhaut
system.description: A young A3V star 25 light-years away encircled by a stunning ring-shaped debris disk. The Hubble Space Telescope captured what appeared to be a planet within the ring, though its nature remains debated.

fomalhaut.name: Fomalhaut
fomalhaut.description: An A3V blue-white main-sequence star surrounded by a bright, asymmetric ring of dust and debris at roughly 140 AU. The ring is offset from the star and has a sharp inner edge — suggesting a planet is shepherding material along a gravitational boundary.
fomalhaut.funFact: Fomalhaut is one of only a few stars whose circumstellar disk was photographed directly by Hubble. The ring's sharp inner edge, pointing to a shepherding planet, made this one of the most compelling pre-directly-imaged exoplanet cases.

fomalhautb.name: Fomalhaut b (Dagon)
fomalhautb.description: A controversial object discovered by Hubble in visible light — originally hailed as the first directly imaged exoplanet. Later observations showed it expanding rather than remaining point-like, leading to the alternative hypothesis that it may be a cloud of dust ejected by an asteroid collision. Its planetary nature remains unresolved.
fomalhautb.funFact: Fomalhaut b was officially named 'Dagon' by the IAU in 2015, after a Semitic deity associated with the sea — but its very existence as a planet is still disputed, making it one of the most enigmatic objects in exoplanet science.
